items.context: @KashKysh (65.538 seguidores), en inglés: ironiza sobre las cold wallets en 2026 (Ledger, Trezor, Coldcard con semillas no aleatorias por 5 años, Tangem) y remata que la cold wallet más segura es no tener cripto. Noticia fresca verificada: Coinkite admitió que el firmware de Coldcard (mar-2021 a jul-2026) usó un RNG débil; Galaxy Research cifra ~1.778 BTC robados. A ~4 h: 34 likes, 4 reposts, 20 respuestas. Conversación activa de custodia donde tu libro calza directo.
items.suggested_text:
The pattern across that list is that almost none of it breaks the idea of cold storage itself. Each case is trust placed in one link of the chain: the reseller, the email channel, or the vendor's random number generator.

Coldcard is the clearest example. From March 2021 to July 2026, affected firmware built seeds on a weak software RNG, with entropy reportedly as low as 40 bits, and attackers rebuilt keys on their own machines without touching a single device. Galaxy Research counts about 1,778 BTC taken. A firmware update doesn't repair a seed that already exists; the only fix is a new seed and moving the funds.

That's why the part of self-custody worth owning is the entropy and the signing process itself, not just the brand of the box. It's the approach I walk through in the book: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

Not owning crypto does remove this risk. It just swaps it for a different one that's harder to see.
